hlido_opinion.headline: PMCP — a versioned, PyPI-packaged MCP gateway with strong release/CI discipline but near-zero adoption so far.
hlido_opinion.body: PMCP (Progressive MCP) is an MCP gateway published to PyPI and cut into tagged releases up to v1.19.3, with five CI workflows and a large 54K-char README — the engineering hygiene here is notably strong for a long-tail project. The gap is adoption: at 15 stars it is effectively pre-traction, so while the packaging and release discipline are real, there is little external signal that it has been battle-tested. That makes it an interesting pick for a team that values a properly versioned, pip-installable gateway and is comfortable being an early adopter. As with every repo-surface review, the 82 reflects repository health — packaging, releases, CI, docs — not the gateway's measured runtime behavior.

tier_rationale: STEADY (82), the repo-surface ceiling: MIT-licensed, PyPI-packaged, tagged releases (v1.19.3), five CI workflows, a 54K-char README, and daily commits. Not VITAL because gateway runtime correctness needs hands-on testing, and adoption is still negligible (15 stars), so real-world hardening is unproven.
what_it_does_well: Proper release discipline — tagged releases up to v1.19.3
Five CI workflows — the strongest automated gating in this batch
MIT-licensed and actively committed (daily at review time)
what_it_fails_at: No external evidence of production hardening
Runtime gateway behavior was not hands-on tested
best_for: Early adopters who want a versioned, pip-installable MCP gateway
Teams that value release/CI discipline over headcount of stars
not_recommended_for: Risk-averse buyers who need a widely-adopted, proven gateway
Anyone who treats star count / community size as a hard requirement

compared_to.verdict_diff: mcp-gateway (PMCP) wins on packaging and release discipline (PyPI + tagged releases + 5 CI workflows); pluggedin-mcp-proxy wins on adoption (132 vs 15 stars) and hub features. Choose based on whether release hygiene or community traction matters more to you.
